title: Petra and the Alibi
premise: Retired detective Oscar Thackeray, now barely keeping her failing bookshop afloat, receives a confession letter for a murder committed thirty years ago — postmarked the day after the victim's funeral, and signed with her late partner's name. Refusing to believe he was guilty, she reopens the cold case of Petra Voss, a young woman whose death was ruled an accident, only to discover that every witness from that night has spent three decades protecting an alibi built on a lie. As she decodes a ledger hidden in the bookshop's own cataloging system — left behind by her partner — she uncovers a conspiracy among the town's founding families who traded justice for survival. At the anniversary dinner where the conspirators gather to finally bury the past, Oscar exposes the true killer: not her partner, but the beloved town matriarch whose confession letter was sent posthumously by an heir seeking absolution. In the end, Oscar must choose between handing the evidence to a compromised police force or letting the town judge its own history.
about_author: Oscar Voss is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who covered unsolved cases for fifteen years before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town much like the one in this novel, where they run a secondhand bookshop that doubles as their writing office.

chapters.title: The Letter After the Funeral
chapters.summary: Oscar Thackeray, dusting unsold stock in her failing bookshop, opens a confession letter signed by her dead partner Elias, confessing to Petra Voss's murder thirty years ago. The postmark is dated the day after his funeral. Her POV. Emotional beat: grief curdling into disbelief and stubborn refusal.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Oscar digs out her old case files and revisits the official ruling: Petra fell from the harbor cliffs after a storm. But the file is thin — too thin, she realizes, because Elias handled it. His POV flashes show him sealing something away. Beat: doubt taking root.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Sorting Elias's donated books, Oscar notices catalog numbers that don't match any system she knows — a cipher keyed to dates. The first decoded entry lists initials and sums of money. Her POV. Beat: the thrill of the hunt returning after years of dormancy.

chapters.title: Widow at the Window
chapters.summary: Oscar visits Maren Voss, Petra's mother, now frail and watchful. Maren insists the case is closed and begs Oscar to let the dead rest. Third-person limited on Oscar. Beat: first hint that someone in town is afraid of more than grief.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Night
chapters.summary: The ledger's first page decodes fully: four names, four payments, dated the night Petra died. All four belong to founding families still prominent in Harrow Bay. Oscar's POV. Beat: the case stops being personal and becomes structural.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Invitation
chapters.summary: An engraved invitation arrives: the thirtieth anniversary dinner honoring Petra, hosted by matriarch Cordelia Ashcombe. Someone wants Oscar in the room. Her POV, laced with dark humor. Beat: the sense of being moved like a piece on a board.

chapters.title: What Elias Kept
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter in Elias's POV, thirty years earlier: the night of Petra's death, what he actually saw at the cliffs, and why he buried it — a choice between his badge and his life. Beat: the price of survival made intimate and terrible.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Burns Slowly
chapters.summary: A small fire damages the shop's back room — precisely where the ledger books were stored. Insurance calls it wiring; Oscar knows better. Her POV. Beat: fear arrives, and with it the confirmation she's right.

chapters.title: The Second Witness
chapters.summary: Oscar tracks down Ruthie Calloway, once Petra's best friend, now living under another name two towns over. Ruthie talks in fragments: a boat, a scream, a man's coat. Beat: the alibi begins to crack along its oldest seam.

chapters.title: Ledger Page Nine
chapters.summary: Decoding continues: page nine records a payment made *after* the death — hush money renewed annually for thirty years, still active. Someone alive is paying. Oscar's POV. Beat: the case turns from history into present danger.

chapters.title: Cordelia's Glass
chapters.summary: Oscar accepts the dinner invitation and pays a preliminary call on Cordelia Ashcombe, who is charming, generous, and utterly unshakeable. Their conversation is a duel of courtesies. Oscar's POV. Beat: meeting the antagonist and liking her against her will.

chapters.title: The Cop Who Owes Her
chapters.summary: Oscar approaches Detective Imani Reyes, a former protégée, hoping to reopen the case officially. Imani warns her the department buried it under pressure from above. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallizes — even the law chose survival.

chapters.title: Ruthie Recants
chapters.summary: Ruthie calls Oscar at midnight, terrified, retracting everything — then goes silent. Oscar finds her motel room emptied. Her POV. Beat: guilt and urgency; the cost of asking questions lands on others.

chapters.title: The Heir's Confession
chapters.summary: Oscar confronts Julian Ashcombe, Cordelia's grandson, who admits he mailed the letter after finding his grandmother's written confession among her papers. He wanted the truth out but lacks the nerve. Beat: the letter's origin solved; the murder's isn't.

chapters.title: What the Confession Says
chapters.summary: Julian shares Cordelia's handwritten account — but it contradicts the ledger on one crucial detail: the time of death. Either Cordelia lied in her confession, or the ledger hides a fifth participant. Oscar's POV. Beat: the ground shifts beneath the whole theory.

chapters.title: Storm Weather
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the night using tide charts, weather logs, and Elias's sealed notes, Oscar proves Petra died hours later than the official record — when all four named suspects had ironclad alibis. Beat: the alibi wasn't covering a murder; it was covering who *didn't* do it.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: The final ledger page, encoded differently, yields a fifth initial: E. Elias didn't just witness — he was paid, the money funding the bookshop itself. Oscar's POV, devastated. Beat: loyalty vs. truth turns inward; her whole life was bought with the lie.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Oscar attends the dinner carrying the decoded ledger. Toasts are raised; Cordelia watches her with knowing calm. Oscar rises and reads the fifth name aloud. Beat: climax ignites — the room becomes a courtroom.

chapters.title: The Truth About Petra
chapters.summary: Under the weight of the assembled evidence, Cordelia confesses publicly: she killed Petra to protect her son, then purchased everyone's silence — including Elias's — believing survival required it. Beat: the villain is fully human; the theme lands hard.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Imani arrives to arrest Cordelia, but the department's old protectors move to bury it again. The townspeople present — descendants of the four names — must decide whether to back the cover-up or the truth. Beat: the community chooses, painfully, to testify.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Cordelia in custody, Julian shattered, Ruthie safe and speaking freely. Oscar sits with Maren Voss, who finally grieves openly, and forgives Elias — mostly. Beat: mourning without absolution; the price tallied honestly.

chapters.title: Open for Business
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Oscar repaints the bookshop front and recatalogs the shelves in plain, honest order — no more ciphers. A new customer brings a fresh mystery wrapped in brown paper. She smiles, and takes the case. Beat: resolution and renewal; the detective lives on.
